title: Rapid response playbook for tenant-isolated capacity shortfalls and scaling regression
creator: Amelia Park
description: Create and validate an actionable rapid-response playbook and short/mid/long-term remediation plan for capacity shortfalls that manifest only for specific tenants (tenant-isolated), and for scaling regressions in the Dedicated autoscaler. The playbook must: 1) enable first responders to identify tenant-scoped capacity starvation vs global fleet issues; 2) provide safe emergency mitigations (traffic reroute, tenant burst shifting, temporary model downgrades) with minimal blast radius; 3) include concrete tuning parameters and rollback criteria for autoscaler rollouts; 4) define postmortem action items and owner assignments.
context: In the last two incidents, a small subset of high-QPS tenants experienced sustained throughput degradation while global fleet metrics appeared healthy. Root cause analysis shows a combination of shard imbalance, autoscaler parameter regressions in node provisioning cooldowns, and slow KV cache warmup for long-lived conversations. Current oncall runbooks assume global capacity problems and often trigger broad-scaled mitigations that increase cost and customer disruption. We need a tenant-aware playbook and technical fixes to avoid repeating this class of incidents.
impact: Multiple enterprise customers reported SLA violations (tail latency and dropped requests) for 30-90 minutes during peak traffic. Revenue-risking tenants were affected; support escalations required manual intervention from oncall. Impact classification: high for affected tenants, medium globally due to increased operator action and cost.
mitigation_steps: Triage: run tenant-scoped KPI query (dashboard: /dashboards/dedicated/tenant-qps) and compare tenant QPS vs pool capacity per-shard
Immediate short-term: enable tenant burst mode for affected tenants (API: POST /admin/tenants/{id}/burst?duration=15m) to shift them into reserved burst capacity pool
If burst mode not sufficient: apply emergency routing to a compatible model variant with lower per-token GPU cost (e.g., v1-mlq -> v1-mlq-2q) and annotate incident
Temporarily lift autoscaler min_shards constraint for specific tenant pools to allow vertical packing (ops flag: autoscaler.min_shards_override={tenant_id}:{value})

If autoscaler regression suspected: revert the last autoscaler config change via config rollback (git rev: refs/heads/autoscaler/config@{1}) and redeploy controller; monitor scaling events for 15 minutes
Collect logs: controller events (/var/logs/autoscaler.log), per-tenant scheduler traces, and kernel-selection histograms from serving nodes (command: curl http://node-metrics/metrics?shard={id})
Communicate: update status page and affected tenant CSMs with ETA and mitigation steps; use incident template in Confluence: /confluence/dedicated/tenant-incident-template
postmortem_actions: Short-term (<=2d): patch autoscaler to block config that increases cooldown beyond 120s without experimental flag; add automated healthcheck that correlates scaling events with per-tenant latency
Short-term: add a dashboard panel for shard imbalance ratio and KV-cache-warmup-rate per-tenant; default alarm threshold set to imbalance_ratio>1.8 for 2m
Mid-term (2-4w): implement tenant QoS layer in routing that enforces per-tenant headroom and isolates burst consumption to avoid noisy neighbor effects
Mid-term: extend autoscaler to support tenant-aware delta scaling (scale-up prioritized by tenant impact score) and introduce a safe mode that requires explicit approval for fleet-wide config changes

Long-term (1-3mo): redesign shard assignment to include tenant affinity and hot-tenant smoothing to reduce cold KV cache penalties; consider model-aware scheduling that prefers quantized variants under tight headroom
Documentation: update oncall runbook with tenant triage checklist and example CLI commands; add playbook to Console runbook library

Ownership: assign follow-ups with owners and deadlines: ENG-518421-A: autoscaler cooldown guard - owner: Rafael Gomez - due 2025-03-10; ENG-518421-B: tenant QoS layer design - owner: Priya Nair - due 2025-04-01
acceptance_criteria: Runbook validated in fire-drill with SRE and two engineers acting as incident commanders
Automated alerts fire for shard imbalance and KV-cache-warmup regressions and are routed to oncall channel #dedicated-ops
Autoscaler config rollback path documented and tested with a canary that reverts within 5 minutes without additional operator steps
Tenant burst API path tested end-to-end and limits are enforced to prevent abuse
